features: Deep ocean trenches — where one plate bends down beneath the other
Volcanic arcs — chains of volcanoes fed by the sinking plate melting
Fold mountain ranges — crust crumpled upward where two continents collide
The strongest earthquakes — the locked, sinking plate slips in great jolts
examples: Nazca under South American - the Andes
Pacific under Philippine Sea - the Mariana Trench

divergent-boundary.crust: new crust is created from rising magma
features: Mid-ocean ridges — underwater mountain chains of freshly made crust
Rift valleys — the land stretched and dropped as a continent begins to split
Shallow earthquakes — small and near the surface, from crust cracking apart
Fissure volcanism — lava welling up through cracks rather than from cones
examples: Mid-Atlantic Ridge - North American from Eurasian
East African Rift - African from Somali
Iceland, where the ridge runs onshore

transform-boundary.motion: plates slide horizontally past each other
transform-boundary.crust: crust is neither created nor destroyed
features: Strike-slip faults — the two sides slide horizontally past each other
Offset ridges and streams — features cut and shifted sideways along the fault
Shallow but destructive earthquakes — near the surface, so they hit hard
No volcanism — nothing melts when plates only grind sideways
examples: San Andreas Fault - Pacific past North American
